art.subject: Brown Shrike (Lanius cristatus cristatus), adult male, as seen on Korean islands and field edges during passage in May and August-September: crown, nape, back and rump plain warm rufous-brown, the crown about the same colour as the back; a narrow white forehead line continuing as a white supercilium above a broad black mask from the lores through the eye to the ear coverts; throat white; underparts creamy-white with a rich rufous-buff wash on the breast sides, flanks and belly; wings dark brown with paler rufous-buff edges and no white patch; long rufous-brown tail; strong blackish hooked bill; dark eye; dark grey legs.
art.pose: perched upright on the top of a shrub, tail slightly lowered, scanning the ground for insects
art.scene: Korean island scrub and field edge with shrubs in May, during spring passage, fresh green leaves; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright on top of a shrub: large head, rufous-brown crown and nape like the russet-brown back, buffish-white lower forehead and white supercilium above a black mask from the lores to the rear ear-coverts, whitish throat, creamy underparts with rufous-buff flanks, brown wings, long rounded tail, stout hooked bill

adult female, side view perched: like the male but paler, the mask blackish-brown and less clean-cut, white supercilium, rufous-brown crown and back, fine dark vermiculation on the creamy breast sides and flanks
art.build: Medium-sized shrike, about the size of a Bull-headed Shrike and larger than a sparrow, with a large head, upright posture and long tail. Bill stout, shorter than the head, deep and laterally compressed with a hooked tip. Legs short, strong, dark grey. Wings short and rounded; the long, graduated, rounded tail extends far beyond the wingtips and is often swung slowly from side to side. Hunts from exposed perches, dropping onto insects.
avoid: Do not paint a pale grey crown - that marks the subspecies lucionensis; in this form the crown is warm rufous-brown like the back.
Do not paint a white patch on the primaries or a rufous crown contrasting with a grey back - those mark Bull-headed Shrike (Lanius bucephalus).
Do not paint black-barred chestnut upperparts with a blue-grey crown (Tiger Shrike, Lanius tigrinus).
Do not make the bill thin or straight; it is stout and hooked.
